title: Israel bombs Houthi-held port of Hodeidah after Tel Aviv drone attack
body:
On 20 July 2024 Israeli warplanes struck the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah in Yemen, causing a large fire and black smoke. The strike came a day after a drone attack on Tel Aviv that killed an Israeli civilian and that Israel attributed to the Houthis, who control much of Yemen.

A Houthi official said the strikes hit fuel storage facilities and a power plant. The Houthi-run health ministry said three people were killed and 87 wounded, most with severe burns, figures that Agence France-Presse could not independently verify. An AFP correspondent reported several large explosions, and a resident described the city as dark with petrol stations closed. The maritime security firm Ambrey reported no damage to merchant vessels at the time.

Defence Minister Yoav Gallant said "the blood of Israeli citizens has a price" and warned of more operations if the Houthis attacked again, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said anyone who harms Israel would pay a heavy price. Military spokesman Daniel Hagari said the Houthis used Hodeidah as a supply route for Iranian weapons, including the drone that hit Tel Aviv. The United States said it was not involved in or coordinating with the strikes, and Saudi Arabia said it had no links to them. Houthi official Mohammed al-Bukhaiti vowed escalation in response.
